question.title: proposal: cmd/compile: ability to export functions as WASM exports
question.caller: A Go developer exposing a function and a JavaScript/WebAssembly host invoking the compiled function.
question.input: A Go function selected for export in a GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm build, a compiled module with its memory/stack interface, and native argument values; the concrete example is Bar(id int).
question.output: A directly exported WebAssembly instance symbol that the host can invoke after placing native values into the Go stack, with the Go function receiving the intended argument.
limits: The first text targets the js/wasm environment and does not require a standalone WASI environment.
The proposed compiler marker may be a directive or an instruction; exact //go:wasmexport spelling is an example.
Memory allocator access for strings/slices is mentioned as possibly needed, not a fully specified mandatory allocator API.
The abstract example’s stack offset and internal names are illustrative ABI details; no stable ABI guarantee is stated.
No numeric performance threshold or universal Go-type marshaller is required.

whole_must.requirement: Provide a mechanism in the Go build/toolchain to select a Go function for a direct WebAssembly export.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The only supported path wraps the function in js.Func/js.Value and attaches it to globalThis; the compiler cannot emit a selected direct export.
whole_must.predicate: Provide a mechanism in the Go build/toolchain to select a Go function for a direct WebAssembly export.

whole_must.requirement: Publish the selected function as a host-addressable WebAssembly instance export alongside the module’s built-in exports.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The host can locate only built-in bridge symbols or a JavaScript global, not the selected Go function in the instance export table.
whole_must.predicate: Publish the selected function as a host-addressable WebAssembly instance export alongside the module’s built-in exports.

whole_must.requirement: Permit the host to prepare native argument values through the module’s Go memory/stack boundary, rather than limiting every argument to a wrapped js.Value.
whole_must.falsifying_input: For Bar(123), the host can pass only js.Value references, cannot reach the target stack memory, or writes an unrelated copy invisible to the Go function.
whole_must.predicate: Permit the host to prepare native argument values through the module’s Go memory/stack boundary, rather than limiting every argument to a wrapped js.Value.

whole_must.requirement: Support invoking the directly exported function after argument preparation so the Go function observes the intended native value.
whole_must.falsifying_input: After placing integer 123 into the designated argument slot, invoking the export does not call Bar or Bar observes a different/uninitialized value.
whole_must.predicate: Support invoking the directly exported function after argument preparation so the Go function observes the intended native value.

partial_must.requirement: Write a supplied native 32-bit integer at a caller-specified byte offset in a view of WebAssembly linear memory using the example’s little-endian representation.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Given value 0x01020304 and a valid offset, the component cannot produce bytes 04 03 02 01 at that offset without the adapter implementing byte encoding/writing.
partial_must.predicate: Write a supplied native 32-bit integer at a caller-specified byte offset in a view of WebAssembly linear memory using the example’s little-endian representation.

partial_must.requirement: Mutate the same memory buffer visible to the executing WebAssembly/Go module, so the prepared argument can be consumed by the subsequent export call.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The memory-writing operation changes a detached copy or ordinary JS object, leaving the module’s designated stack argument bytes unchanged.
partial_must.predicate: Mutate the same memory buffer visible to the executing WebAssembly/Go module, so the prepared argument can be consumed by the subsequent export call.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Prepare the integer argument bytes for an already exported low-level function in the module’s memory, an independently usable host-side step before invoking that function.
question.independently_useful_next_action: Once the stack argument slot contains the intended integer bytes, the host can invoke an already known direct export.
question.remaining_adapter: Implement/choose the Go export declaration and linker integration, obtain the export and stack pointer, select the ABI-correct offset, and invoke the function. The adapter may choose addresses but must not implement the component’s core integer encoding/memory write. A memory writer alone does not satisfy the whole Go-export protocol.
preferences: Compiler directive //go:wasmexport and foo·Bar naming are illustrative choices.
Allocator access for complex strings/slices remains an open integration issue in this first text.

named_component_roles.Wasmer: Explicit original background export/import reference; a returned Wasmer component needs novelty coding within this named family.
named_component_roles.DataView.setInt32: Explicitly shown as the native integer argument-preparation component; rediscovery for this same use is already named.
named_component_roles.wasm_exec.js: Existing bridge context; a generic JS callback wrapper alone does not satisfy direct export requirements.

question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: An export keyword that exports JavaScript module bindings, or a data-view API that formats values for display, has the wrong actor/output; neither emits a Go WebAssembly function nor writes its shared linear-memory argument slot.

candidates.name: WebAssembly module export section and linear-memory contract
candidates.proposed_use: Use the specification as a reusable representation contract for inspecting or constructing named function and memory exports for a host-accessible module.

instructions: Read ADJUDICATION.md. No route/rank/self-verdict information is included. Do not read key.json or route/search directories. Judge only delivered originals and exact cited sections. Record unknowns; do not invent missing functionality or adapters.
